cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage, scaling with Stamina spent, then heal 2 per Stamina.

upgrade.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage, scaling with Stamina spent, then heal 3 per Stamina.

cards.name: Blight Nova
cards.flavor:
Reading of every name, aloud and at once.

Composed by the Furnace Saint after the Burning. The novices say it is what the fire did that night, and that the rite exists so it will be remembered. The remnant holds it holiest of the liturgies.

It has never been performed to its end.
cards.textTemplate: Deal damage equal to twice the target's Crimson Blight.

upgrade.textTemplate: Deal damage equal to three times the target's Crimson Blight.

cards.name: Last Rites
cards.flavor:
Rite for those not to be written.

Foreigners, criminals, and in the last years, the bought-marked of whom the Chapel had not been told. The rubric forbids a name upon the headstone, and calls this discretion.

The lower cemetery stands blank by the thousand.
cards.textTemplate: Heal 20% of your max HP. Draw {draw} cards. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Heal 20% of your max HP. Draw {draw} cards.

cards.name: Zealotry
cards.flavor:
Creed of the Feral Ember.

Each wound is a door the fire walks through. Its priests bless wounds rather than bind them, and hold that the Chapel knew as much, and hid it behind a ledger.

Its converts do not live long. More come each week.
cards.textTemplate: Whenever you lose HP, deal 3 damage to a random enemy.

cards.name: Blood Harvest
cards.flavor:
Reaping of the field of the marked.

So the liturgy names the gathering of names at the close of a plague year. The Saints went out with sickles and ledgers, and the rite is spoken throughout as thanksgiving.

We reap the field of the marked, and give thanks.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies, scaling with Stamina spent. Then heal 3 per Stamina.

upgrade.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies, scaling with Stamina spent. Then heal 3 per Stamina.

cards.name: Pain Offering
cards.flavor:
Small pain, offered in advance.

Taught to crown-born children as good citizenship; the children called it paying early. The habit outlived the Chapel among the Forsaken hamlets, learned from refugees after the Burning.

They keep it without knowing whom they pay.
cards.textTemplate: Lose {loseHp} HP. Deal {damage} damage.

cards.name: Withering Touch
cards.flavor:
Touch that withers growth.

Permitted by the rubric upon the weeds of the weald's field-shrines, and nothing else. In the years the Field Flame dimmed, a clause was added forbidding its use upon crops.

The clause is dated after three harvests had failed, and signed by a Saint absent from the roll of Saints.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {crimsonBlight} Crimson Blight.

cards.name: Desperate Rite
cards.flavor:
Rite for when the bier is already made.

The rubric bids the officiant pray louder, and nothing more. The Saints held that the fire heeds the strength of a voice; the novices, that the rubric was written for the family.

The Herald has performed it upon themselves.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. If below half HP: deal {damage.2} instead.

cards.name: Ember Tide
cards.flavor:
The Chapel's name for the night of the Burning.

The night the fire read the names of the crown-born all at once. The novices say the censers swung untouched through it, as the congregation burned around them. The censers of the Furnace Chapel have not stopped since.

We kept the censer swinging when the hearth went dark.
cards.textTemplate: Whenever you heal, gain 1 Strength.

cards.name: Blood Offering
cards.flavor:
Bowl filled with the officiant's own blood.

From the Chapel's first years, when the Saints were few; revived by the Furnace Saint after the Burning, when they were fewer. He performs it daily, and grows thin.

The bowl is always full.
cards.textTemplate: Lose {loseHp} HP. Deal {damage} damage.

cards.name: Harbinger of Blight
cards.flavor:
Title of the Feral Ember's preachers.

The Chapel gave the same name to the novice who walked before a bier with a bell. The Feral Ember holds that the word was never the Chapel's to give, but the fire's.

We go before the fire, and it follows us gladly.
cards.textTemplate: Whenever Crimson Blight is applied to an enemy, heal 1 HP.

cards.name: Blightward Lash
cards.flavor:
Scourge turned upon one's own rot.

A discipline the Herald took up after the Burning: to cut the Blight from their own flesh and turn it outward. The Chapel remnant condemns it as heresy against the fire's gift.

Twice the remnant has sent a novice to ask how it is done.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {crimsonBlight} Crimson Blight. Lose {loseHp} HP.

cards.name: Last Mercy
cards.flavor:
Warming of a dying hand.

The Chapel's nursing sisters did it with a coal wrapped in cloth, that the fire might find the hand gentle. The Wandering Physician learned it from them, and does it without the coal.

It seems to work as well. He cannot say what working means.
cards.textTemplate: Heal {heal} HP. Gain {block} Block.

cards.name: Warm Litany
cards.flavor:
First prayer of the Furnace Chapel's novices.

Said over a small hurt, to keep it warm. The novices were taught its words were older than the Chapel, found by the first Saint cut into the caldera wall.

We give the name. We keep the warmth.
cards.textTemplate: Heal {heal}. Gain {block} Block.

cards.name: Ambush
cards.flavor:
Opening of the frozen docks.

Strike from beneath a bridge, from behind, before the other has decided there is a fight at all. The docks learned it from the Court's surgeons, who walked the bridges by night with their bags, and always arrived first.

Their day-books record house calls, but no houses.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Prepared: deal {damage.2} more. Apply {vulnerable} Vulnerable. Consume Prepared.

cards.name: Shiv
cards.flavor:
Sliver of iron from the rail of the Fourth Bridge.

The ironwork froze brittle the night the Court Flame died. Dock children say the railings were cast from the Court's melted oath-tokens, and so are worth more than any blade in the right hands.

Whose hands are right, the children will not tell.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Exhaust.

cards.name: Smoke Pellet
cards.flavor:
Tallow and ash, rolled in a back room on the Chandlers' Stair.

Sold as lamp-starters. The chandler says the recipe was his grandmother's, taken from a Court surgeon, though in his telling the surgeon is sometimes a knight.

The docks buy more of them each winter.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Become Prepared. Exhaust.

cards.name: Quick Cut
cards.flavor:
Knife-work of the Tollmouth fence.

He pays only for quick cuts, holding that a slow cut is a confession and a quick one an accident. Before the Decree, a dock child caught with a knife was hanged, not branded.

The fence considers that the better age.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Prepared: deal {damage.2} more. Consume Prepared.

cards.name: Feint
cards.flavor:
Oldest trick of the frozen docks.

Eyes on the purse, hand on the knife. The docks say the Court's knights were easily taken, for they had sworn to look wherever a threat was declared.

No such clause appears in their oath-book. The knights wrote the oath-book.
cards.textTemplate: Become Prepared. Draw {draw} card.

upgrade.textTemplate: Become Prepared. Draw {draw} card. Gain {block} Block.

cards.name: Backstep
cards.flavor:
Retreat of the lower-river ice-cutters.

The cutters know which ice beneath the bridges holds and which only seems to, and sell the knowledge by the season. Their map is drawn inside a cutter's coat and passed down with it.

Its present wearer says it has been wrong since the second winter.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Become Prepared.

cards.name: Twin Prick
cards.flavor:
Two small wounds, set close together.

The Court's surgeons recorded them as bites when they found them upon bodies along the bridges. Their receipts give the hour, the bridge and the fee for the inquest. Not one case was closed.

The dock children call it the Surgeon's Signature.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage {hits} times. Prepared: deal {damage.2} damage {hits.2} times. Consume Prepared.

cards.name: Pocket Sand
cards.flavor:
Kiln ash, carried in a coat lining.

From the south-bank lime kilns, where the dock poor laboured for the Court's builders. The Court paid in lime and taxed in coin; the ash was the one thing given freely.

The kilns went cold with the Court Flame. The ash has not run out.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Apply {weak} Weak.

cards.name: Hamstring
cards.flavor:
Cut behind the knee.

The docks' answer to the stitched knights, who cannot kneel, and once fallen cannot rise. The surgeons called the knights unbending. On the docks, the word is taken as written.

The Fourth Bridge rail bears a tally of knights left upon the ice.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {vulnerable} Vulnerable.

cards.name: Serrated Shiv
cards.flavor:
Shiv sawn from a Marionette's spine-rod.

The Court's surgeons set steel rods in the spines of their dancers, to keep them upright through the dance. Dock thieves call the taking of one a mercy.

The surgeons who fitted them took their reasons beneath the ice.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {bleed} Bleed. Prepared: apply {bleed.2} more. Consume Prepared.

cards.name: Smoke Veil
cards.flavor:
River fog, thickened with ash.

The fog rose off the water the night the Court Flame died, and has not lifted. The Court's lamplighters, paid to burn it away, were the first to be lost in it.

Their guild-book ends with a list of lamps to be relit. None are marked done.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Apply {weak} Weak to ALL enemies.

cards.name: Ricochet
cards.flavor:
Blade skipped across the ice.

A children's game on the frozen river, played with pebbles by the young and knives by the old. The ice keeps no witnesses, they say.

It is said the Marrow Organist, beneath it, hears every throw.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies.

cards.name: Low Blow
cards.flavor:
Strike below the belt.

Forbidden by the Court's code of arms, which hangs upon the Citadel gate in frost-bitten gilt. The children of the docks read it aloud to one another in jest.

Its final clause, on the treatment of the unmarked, has been chipped from the stone.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage. Prepared: deal {poiseDamage.2} more Poise damage. Consume Prepared.

cards.name: Pilfer
cards.flavor:
Lift worked in the crowds upon the bridges.

The Court counted wrists and kept careful rolls, but never counted purses. Old Keel, the Tollmouth fence, taught that to rob a courtier sewn to his post was salvage, not theft.

He claimed to have been a courtier once. His wrist bears the brand.
cards.textTemplate: Draw {draw} cards. Discard 1 card at random.

cards.name: Vanish
cards.flavor:
Art of the unmarked beneath the bridges.

Taught to the docks by those who lived under the Citadel's bridges before the Decree, when to be seen was to be entered on a roll. Under the bridges there is nothing but ice.

Most of those teachers vanished in the end. Where to, the docks cannot agree.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Become Prepared. Add a Smoke Pellet to your hand. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Become Prepared. Add a Smoke Pellet to your hand.

cards.name: Cheap Shot
cards.flavor:
Blow at the already wounded.

The Tollmouth fence calls it the only honest bargain on the river, and charges for lessons in teeth. He says he learned the practice from a Court magistrate who levied fines the same way.

The jar upon his counter is nearly full.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. If the target is Weak, deal {damage.2} more.

cards.name: Blade Dance
cards.flavor:
Cuts in the figure of the Marionettes' dance.

The surgeons stitched the Court's dancers to their dance when the Court Flame died, and they perform upon the frozen river for no one. The dance was meant to end at dawn.

A small Marionette on the Fourth Bridge waits for the ending. Thieves leave her coins.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage {hits} times. Prepared: deal {damage.2} damage {hits.2} times. Consume Prepared.

cards.name: Garrote
cards.flavor:
Loop of the Court tailors' gilt thread.

Bought cheap on the docks once the tailors had no more use for it. The Court's surgeons bought the same thread, for purposes never shared with the tailors.

The surgeons and the stranglers were ever its best customers.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {bleed} Bleed and {weak} Weak.

cards.name: Fan of Knives
cards.flavor:
Surgeon's roll of scalpels, thrown as one.

The rolls reach the docks more often than their owners, sold by ice-cutters who find them frozen into the river, the coat still about them. The surgeons tried to flee the Citadel on the night of the Burning.

The ice closed over those who ran.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies. Draw {draw} card.

cards.name: Setup
cards.flavor:
Preparation of a dock job.

A window left open on the Lantern Bridge, a lamp turned low, a guard paid to cough. The method is credited to a thief called the Wick, who planned the first robbery of the Regent's hall in the years of the Mark Trade.

It is said the Court itself paid her to rob it.
cards.textTemplate: Become Prepared. Gain {gainEnergy} Stamina. Add a Shiv to your hand. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Become Prepared. Gain {gainEnergy} Stamina. Draw {draw} card. Add a Shiv to your hand. Exhaust.

cards.name: Acrobatics
cards.flavor:
The rooftop road of the frozen docks.

Bridge rail, lamp post, gutter, never the street. The Court's watch walked only the paved ways, for the paving had been blessed at the Founding and the rooftops had not.

Whether the watch was pious or idle is not agreed.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Draw {draw} cards. Discard 1 at random.

cards.name: Disorient
cards.flavor:
Spin practised in the Hall of Mirrors.

The Glass Regent's mirrors are the frozen river beneath the bridges, and they show more than stands before them. Thieves who went in for the silver learned to turn a courtier until he lost the throne.

It is said the Regent herself now reigns from the wrong side of the glass.
cards.textTemplate: Apply {weak} Weak and {vulnerable} Vulnerable. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Apply {weak} Weak and {vulnerable} Vulnerable.

cards.name: Coup de Grace
cards.flavor:
Finishing thrust of the Court's surgeons.

They called it a courtesy and billed it as a procedure, listed between stitching and funeral in their fee schedule. The docks learned it watching the surgeons at work upon the bridges after the Burning.

The schedule has since been amended by hand. The price has risen.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. If the target is Vulnerable, deal {damage.2} more.

cards.name: Sap
cards.flavor:
Sand-weighted cosh of the docks.

Meant to fell without killing. It does not work upon the Marionettes, who dance on with slack strings. One thief used it upon a girl at the foot of the Stitched Throne, a dancer no older than a dock child.

He returned asking whether anyone knew the tune she hummed.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {weak} Weak. Deal {poiseDamage} Poise damage.

cards.name: Shadowstep
cards.flavor:
Step through a pier's shadow.

The shadows beneath the bridges are let by the season, and rent is owed to whoever held the pier before. Tenancies pass down like a trade.

The oldest belongs to one not seen since the Decree. The rent is always paid.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Become Prepared. Draw {draw} card.

cards.name: Afterimage
cards.flavor:
Reflection left in the Regent's glass.

The mirrors of the Hall held a thief's image a heartbeat longer than they should. The Regent's stewards recorded it as the Hall's loyalty.

The glass has grown slower with each winter since the Burning.
cards.textTemplate: Every third card you play grants 3 Block.

cards.name: Bloodletter
cards.flavor:
Bleeding, as the Citadel's surgeons practised it.

Their receipts name the patient, the measure drawn, and the patient's satisfaction, marked on every surviving copy. The surgeons held that bleeding balanced a courtier's humours before an oath.

Receipts from the last month before the Burning bear no names.
cards.textTemplate: Double the target's Bleed. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Double the target's Bleed.

cards.name: Venomcoat
cards.flavor:
Sedative paste of the Court's surgeons.

Sold by the vial to courtiers who could not sleep in the weeks before the Decree. The docks found it served a blade as well as a cup of wine.

The label promises a dreamless night.
cards.textTemplate: Apply {venom} Venom. Become Prepared.

cards.name: Misdirect
cards.flavor:
Art of leading the watch astray.

Perfected on the night of the Courtly Decree, when the brand-men came down to the river to mark the last of the unmarked by dawn, and the ice-cutters paid the bridge watch to lead them in circles.

The Decree said dawn. On that side of the river, dawn came late.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Apply {weak} Weak to ALL enemies. Become Prepared.

cards.name: Assassinate
cards.flavor:
Killing blow, struck after a single question.

The way of a dock thief who hunts one particular Court surgeon. The question has been told upon the docks; the surgeon's name has not. Some believe the question concerns a stitching. Others, that the surgeon is kin.

The docks have learned not to ask twice.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Prepared: deal {damage.2} more. Consume Prepared. Exhaust.

cards.name: Thousand Cuts
cards.flavor:
Many small cuts, each undoing a stitch.

The surgeons called it the procedure run backward, and forbade it, for a courtier sewn to his post had sworn an oath. The winter after the Burning, a surgeon was found unstitching his own wife from the palace stair.

The surgeons' day-book records only a failed stitching.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage {hits} times. Prepared: deal {damage.2} damage {hits.2} times. Consume Prepared.

cards.name: Deadly Tempo
cards.flavor:
Rhythm of the frozen docks.

The dock clock froze at the Burning, its hands upon the King's Hour. Before, thieves timed their work by it, and the Court timed its watch by the same.

Since then the docks keep time by their own pulses, and no two agree.
cards.textTemplate: At the start of your turn, become Prepared and draw a card.

cards.name: Opportunist
cards.flavor:
First law of the frozen docks.

When the knight stumbles, the purse swings. The stitched knights stumble often in their sewn armour, and the docks have prospered by it.

Many of those knights are the fathers and brothers of the docks. This is not spoken of.
cards.textTemplate: Whenever an enemy Staggers, become Prepared and draw a card.

cards.name: Envenom
cards.flavor:
Poison from a surgeon's second shelf.

The second shelf held what the first could not treat. Thieves who entered the surgeons' houses after the Burning found the second shelves full and the first bare.

The apprentices will not say which was emptied first.
cards.textTemplate: Your attacks apply 1 Venom per stack.

cards.name: Toxic Volley
cards.flavor:
Sedative vials, broken into the river fog.

Loosed upwind of the bridge watch, which slept through three robberies. The river smelled of it for weeks.

The watch ledger records those weeks as quiet, and commends the men for their vigilance.
cards.textTemplate: Apply {venom} Venom and {weak} Weak to ALL enemies.

cards.name: Smoke Bomb
cards.flavor:
Pig's bladder of kiln ash.

Split upon the stones, it raises a fog the bridge watch reports as a haunting. The ash is from the south-bank kilns, which in the Court's last years were fired with something other than lime.

The reports are not wholly wrong.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Apply {weak} Weak to ALL enemies. Exhaust.

cards.name: Execution Window
cards.flavor:
The moment the watch looks away.

Every guard has one. In the years of the Mark Trade, the watch's were written into the roster for a fee: the hours each bridge would stand unguarded, and beside each hour, a name.

None of those names appear in any Court record.
cards.textTemplate: Apply {vulnerable} Vulnerable. Become Prepared. Draw {draw} card. Exhaust.

cards.name: Perfect Heist
cards.flavor:
Theft of the Glass Regent's mirrors.

Every mirror is entered in the Hall's inventory, and every one is gone. The older thieves credit the Wick.

The Hall of Mirrors is full of glass to this day. That is how the docks know it was perfect.
cards.textTemplate: Draw {draw} cards. Gain {gainEnergy} Stamina. Exhaust.

cards.name: Deathblow
cards.flavor:
Killing stroke of the frozen docks.

Struck where the river keeps what the surgeons leave. The river does not thaw, the docks say, because it is full, and the Court built more bridges rather than ask why.

Beneath the ice the Marrow Organist plays the funeral service. He has never reached its end.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. If the target has Bleed, deal {damage.2} more. If it has Venom, deal {damage.3} more.

cards.name: Prepare
cards.flavor:
Hands warmed before the work.

Cold hands drop knives. Dock children learn to warm their hands before they learn to steal, and never at a fire another has lit. A borrowed fire is a debt, and the docks collect.

The fires on the Citadel side burn more than wood.
cards.textTemplate: Become Prepared. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Become Prepared.

cards.name: Pinning Shot
cards.flavor:
An arrow through the hem, not the heart.

Dock archers learned it on the gulls first, then on the Court's bailiffs, whose long coats caught on every piling. A pinned bailiff is a patient one.

The docks still tell which bailiff wore the longest coat, and laugh.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {weak} Weak.

cards.name: Arrow Volley
cards.flavor:
Loose, nock, loose again.

The dock crews kept a barrel of salvaged arrows beneath every stair, few of them straight. A volley did not need them straight, only many and quick, and the crews were both.

The barrels are empty now. Nobody admits to refilling them.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies {hits} times.

cards.name: Nock and Wait
cards.flavor:
The string drawn, the breath held.

A dock archer waits for the tide bell, when every head on the quay turns at once. The bell has rung at the wrong hours since the Burning.

The archers have learned to wait for the heads instead.
cards.textTemplate: Draw {draw} cards. Become Prepared.

cards.name: Aimed Shot
cards.flavor:
One arrow, one seam in the armour.

The stitched knights of the Court wear plate sewn at the joints, and the stitching is the weak place. A dock archer who knows a surgeon's work knows where to aim.

Some of them learned it on the surgeons' tables.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Prepared: deal {damage.2} more and apply {vulnerable} Vulnerable. Consume Prepared.

cards.name: Barbed Arrow
cards.flavor:
A head filed backward so it will not come out.

Fishhook smiths on the docks made them in secret, for the Court forbade barbs after a bailiff died of one. The smiths still make fishhooks.

The fish on the docks are said to be larger than they were.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {bleed} Bleed.

cards.name: Binding Parry
cards.flavor:
The blade caught, turned, and held aside.

A duelling master of the Court taught it for coin to anyone who asked, dock thieves among them. When the Court learned whom he had taught, it stitched his hands.

He teaches it still, by describing it.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Become Prepared. Draw {draw} card.

cards.name: Whirling Guard
cards.flavor:
A spin that is both parry and cut.

Dock dancers performed it for the Court at feast days, with painted wooden knives. After the Burning they were seen performing it on the quay, with other knives, and without the paint.

No feast has been held since.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Deal {damage} damage {hits} times.

cards.name: Draw Cut
cards.flavor:
Single cut from the scabbard, as it is done beyond the marches.

The curved blades reached the ring in the years of the Mark Trade, borne by foreign lords who paid to be warm there. They burned with the rest of the marked, far from home, and left their swords where they fell.

The merchant knows whose each one was. He sells that separately.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {bleed} Bleed.

cards.name: Sundering Hew
cards.flavor:
Hew of a Court knight's greatsword.

Too heavy to carry far, and too dear to leave. The corrupted knights pause at the sight of one in a Forsaken's hands, unable to believe an unmarked hand holds their steel.

That pause is worth the weight.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage.

cards.name: Honed Edge
cards.flavor:
Whetstone from the cairn.

At the Grave of the Nameless, the custom is to take one and leave one. The stones are weald sandstone, marches slate, black glass of the reach. One is starstone.

Within the year, someone always carries it back.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {strength} Strength. Exhaust.

cards.name: Iron Skin
cards.flavor:
Plate of cold iron, worn where a flame-mark would lie.

First worn by the ice-fishers of the Pale Marches in the year of the Decree, when the Court's brand-men came for the unmarked. Such plates are left upon the Grave of the Nameless for those who climb after.

Most have been worn thin by more than one wearer.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block.

cards.name: Field Dressing
cards.flavor:
Clean rag, tied to the cairn.

Boiled by someone who expected to need it, and did not return for it. The custom reached the hamlets with Chapel refugees after the Burning; the hamlets kept the custom, and let the prayer go.

Some rags arrive embroidered with names. The hamlets unpick them.
cards.textTemplate: Heal {heal} HP. Exhaust.

cards.name: Hex
cards.flavor:
Sign scratched upon a door.

The hamlets mark it on houses where someone marked burns slowly within, to keep it from coming out. They learned the sign from the Chapel, which set it upon the houses of the unmarked before the Decree.

The hamlets call it fair to use it the other way round.
cards.textTemplate: Apply {weak} Weak and {vulnerable} Vulnerable. Exhaust.

cards.name: Transmute
cards.flavor:
Cinder spent in the palm.

For a moment, the hand that holds it does not shake. The hamlets hold that each cinder was someone once, and forbid spending a cinder one took oneself.

Those who return from the ring have mostly broken that rule.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {gainEnergy} Stamina. Draw {draw} card. Exhaust.

cards.name: Twin Fang
cards.flavor:
Two knives, worn crosswise.

One for the hound, one for its handler. The weald's blight-hounds were the Wardens' before the Burning, and run yet with Bastion kennelmen who turned with the pack.

A handler may be reasoned with, briefly. Never twice.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage {hits} times.

cards.name: Blinding Sand
cards.flavor:
Ash thrown in the eyes.

The hamlets learned in the first winter that what came out of the weald flinched from ash as the living do. Some took this as proof the corrupted could be saved.

Marl's Hollow took it as proof they could be blinded. Marl's Hollow endures.
cards.textTemplate: Apply {weak} Weak to ALL enemies. Exhaust.

cards.name: Hamstring
cards.flavor:
Cut at the back of the leg.

Taught upon the road with a single instruction: all things of the ring walk, so go for the legs. The saying is scratched on cairns from the weald to the coast, weeks apart.

It is cut in the same hand on every one.
cards.textTemplate: Apply {vulnerable} Vulnerable to ALL enemies. Exhaust.

cards.name: Master of Strategy
cards.flavor:
Maps scratched upon cairn stones.

Left by climbers who came back down, or meant to. The hamlet councils copy the true ones and burn the rest, and each winter argue which were which.

The oldest shows a fourth road leading off the ring toward the coast. It has not been burned.
cards.textTemplate: Draw {draw} cards. Exhaust.

cards.name: Bashing Blow
cards.flavor:
Blow of whatever is heavy.

A cudgel, a mallet, a shovel from a mine camp. The reach's miners swing it at things in the lower galleries that were miners once. Foreman Coll says not to look at their hands, which remember the work.

His camp has lost fewer than any other.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage.

cards.name: Quick Guard
cards.flavor:
Arm raised upon the viaduct.

The viaducts are older than the kingdom, and have no rails. Climbers say they were built to carry heat, not people. Those who cross learn to keep one arm raised against the wind.

The stone has never learned to expect feet.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Draw {draw} card. Exhaust.

cards.name: Sweeping Blow
cards.flavor:
Wide swing for the viaduct.

Where the corrupted come three abreast and the stone is narrow. The Forsaken councils teach that the viaducts were always built to funnel something, long before there were corrupted to funnel.

The corrupted walk them because the stone expects a crowd.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies.

cards.name: Enfeeble
cards.flavor:
Sea salt, rubbed into a wound.

The ship-breakers swear by it. Salt, they say, is the one thing upon the ring the fire has never touched, for nothing written survives the sea.

They have not seen what the Tidebound Abbey keeps in its boathouse.
cards.textTemplate: Apply {vulnerable} Vulnerable to ALL enemies. Exhaust.

cards.name: Colossus Smash
cards.flavor:
Blow at the joints of something vast.

Learned against the Goldbough Avatar, the heraldic idol kneeling in a clearing of the weald, a sapling grown through it. It does not know the kingdom is gone.

It is carved stone and gilt. It flinches all the same.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {vulnerable} Vulnerable.

cards.name: Wound
cards.textTemplate: Unplayable.
cards.flavor:
A cut that closed wrong.

It knits into a hard ridge that aches before the weather turns. Climbers call it the road keeping its share.

The hamlets' older word for it means owed.

cards.name: Dazed
cards.textTemplate: Unplayable. Ethereal.
cards.flavor:
Light behind the eyes, left by a Grave Wisp.

Those who have seen a wisp up close say it looked at them as if reading.

Close your eyes. Do not speak your name until the light is gone.

cards.name: Slimed
cards.textTemplate: Exhaust.
cards.flavor:
Grey muck from the drowned hamlet.

It clings, and will not wash out in cold water. The hamlet flooded before the Burning, in a flood the Wardens called natural.

It is warmer than anything in the weald has a right to be.

cards.name: Guilt
cards.textTemplate: Unplayable. At the end of your turn, if this is in your hand, lose {loseHp} HP.
cards.flavor:
What follows looting at the Second Cairn.

The second time is easier. That is how climbers know the ring has begun on them.

cards.name: Rallying Banner
cards.textTemplate: An ally gains {block} Block.
cards.flavor:
Blank rag upon a pole.

Planted where climbers who meet upon the road may find one another. The Forsaken never had banners, for a banner bears a name. The corrupted come to them too.

A rag on a pole. Find it. Stand by it.

cards.name: Shared Flame
cards.textTemplate: An ally heals {heal} HP. Exhaust.
cards.flavor:
Warmth passed between two climbers.

Hands over one coal, breath beneath one coat, with no hearth and no ledger. The Chapel would have named it theft. It is the only warmth upon the ring owed to no one.

Warmth passed between two outlives the fire.

cards.name: Oath of Ash
cards.textTemplate: An ally gains {strength} Strength; you gain {strength.2}. Exhaust.
cards.flavor:
Oath sworn in ash.

A smear upon each other's wrist, where the mark would have been; no witness, no name. It binds twice, once for each. The Court held that an unwitnessed oath binds no one.

The Court is sewn to its oaths now.

cards.name: Guardian
cards.flavor:
Kite shield of the Court's knights, its strap cut short.

Such shields lie easily found upon the marches road, where the knights who bore them were stitched to their posts and left standing. Climbers take the shields and leave the knights.

The knights have not objected.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Add a temporary Enter: Bulwark to your hand. It costs 1 Stamina and Exhausts. Exhaust.

cards.name: Enter: Bulwark
cards.flavor:
The Wardens' holding stance, learned from the shield.

A shield that stood in the Bastion's line keeps the habit, the elders say, and pulls the arm into place. They call it superstition.

They tell climbers to carry Bastion shields, and never Court ones.
cards.textTemplate: Enter Bulwark Stance. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Enter Bulwark Stance. Gain {block} extra Block. Exhaust.

cards.name: Bastion
cards.flavor:
Tower shield from the Bastion's walls.

Heavy as a door, nearly as tall. The Wardens set such shields in the embrasures to fight from, never to carry. Climbers carry them regardless, for a moving wall is better than a still one.

The weight bows the bearer forward, as the Wardens once bowed before the Bastion.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Gain {weak} Weak. Exhaust.

cards.name: Spiked Reprisal
cards.flavor:
Shield with nails driven through the boss.

The nails are from the Bastion's own gates. It is said a sellsword made it on the night of the Burning, from the gate he was hired to hold. His name is not known.

No bearer since has drawn the nails.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Deal {damage} damage. Apply {bleed} Bleed.

cards.flavor:
Frost spear of the Pale Marches.

Its point was reforged from the broken blade of a Court knight, and marches steel keeps its frost long after leaving the cold. The ice-fishers who made it say the knight gave the blade freely, before the Decree, for a winter's fish.

The ice-fishers keep no records.
cards.name: Rime Thrust
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {frost} Frost.

cards.flavor:
Axe of the Dead Foundry.

The Foundry's fires went out with the Crown Flame, and its forges have been warm ever since, though none has lit them. Corran, a foundryman, broke this axe from a cold mould at dawn and carried it up the Basalt Stair.

He says no one poured it.
cards.name: Kiln Cleave
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {burn} Burn. Deal {poiseDamage} Poise damage.

cards.flavor:
Ward of the Chapel's evening bell-ringers.

A chime rung at vespers to close the day. Its bell was taken long ago; only the frame and the ward remain. Climbers who carry it say it rings at dusk regardless.

A Chapel ward, rung at vespers. The bell is gone.
cards.name: Vesper Ward
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Gain {regen} Regen. Exhaust.

profiles.flavor:
Blow of the empty fist.

The last thing a Forsaken owns once the blade is broken and the cairn has kept it. No hamlet teaches it; it is learned the first winter a sword is traded for salt.

A last resort, still yours.

Rim-blow of the Bastion's shield line.

Climbers learn it from salvaged Warden shields, once gilded with the branch. Most scrape the gold away. The corrupted Wardens of the Fell Courtyard hesitate at the sight of it.

Some leave the gold.

Plain cut of Bastion steel.

Drilled into the field levies and the sellswords hired beside them. Weald smiths never signed their blades, a custom the Chapel's scribes thought insolent and never ended.

Unsigned steel can be carried without anyone asking whose it was.

Turning flurry of the Citadel's midwinter masque.

Court dancers spun double-ended blades before the throne. Stitched to their posts when the Court Flame died, some turn yet upon the frozen river, slower each winter.

Climbers learn the step by watching. The dancers do not mind.

Two quick openings, as the Court's surgeons let a vein.

Their apprentices taught it on the docks once the Court stopped paying them. One teaches it yet, for cinders, beneath the ice below the Citadel.

He learned to open people. He taught himself to close them, and does not sell that part.

Shot loosed from low cover.

The way weald poachers took the deer the Bastion kept for its tables. The Bastion hanged poachers, so the hamlets loosed upon the dawn peal, which hid the sound of the string.

The Bell Keeper rings the peal yet, though no dawn follows.

Cold light struck from an apprentice's staff.

Cut green from weald lanternwood and tipped with starstone bought from the reach miners. The Starwatch taught that the light came from the stone.

It came more easily with the staff turned skyward. The apprentices were told not to notice.

Working of a cantor's sceptre.

Chapel sceptres bore script copied from sealstone doors older than the Chapel. The cantors were taught its sounds, never its sense. The Chapel called the script sacred.

Among themselves, the cantors called it borrowed.

Empty-handed guard of the ice-fishers.

Weight low, feet wide, upon lakes that crack all winter and hold but one at a time. The fishers of Sallow Lake say the ice has a temper, and may be reasoned with.

Those who said otherwise are beneath it.

Haft-turn of the Bastion's field levies.

Sergeant Ilse drilled it upon the Muster Stair. On quiet nights her voice carries from the Bastion walls, calling the count.

The levies she drilled are corrupted now. When they hear her, they take their places.

Shield set against the blow, as the Wardens taught.

Bastion shields bore strips of bell-bronze upon the rim, cast from metal left when the great bell was founded. The Wardens said the bronze rang the hour when struck.

It rings at other hours too.

Ward drawn through a staff, taught upon Starwatch Terrace.

Where the apprentices measured the new tower's draw across the water. The Astronomer said the ward was against the salt wind.

It leaned toward the Spire whenever it was drawn.

Ward of the bier-watch.

Cantors held a sceptre crosswise over the dead through the night, before a name was written. The Chapel taught that it kept the name from wandering.

Where a name might wander, the rubric does not say.

Art of the empty hand.

Mostly the art of not being where the blow lands, taught by the ship-breakers upon hulls that shift with the tide. Gull-Bet calls it the first thing the Forsaken ever had that the marked envied.

That has been true for a very short while.

A weapon learned as it was last used.

Take up what the corrupted drop, and let its habits show. A blade taken from a Warden cuts like a Warden. Orla of the hamlets below the Bastion bears a sword that dips toward the Fell Courtyard as she passes.

She no longer fights the pull.

The poacher's pause before loosing.

Breath out, hand set, wait for the bell. Weald poachers learned patience from the Bastion's gamekeepers, who hanged the impatient. The gamekeepers walk the lanternwood yet, among the corrupted.

They count beneath their breath. The count never ends.

Breath set behind the focus.

Counted to the rhythm of the star tables, recited until the rhythm lived in the breath. The Starwatch taught the tables were only numbers; the apprentices held the rhythm older.

On the night of the eclipse, the Astronomer read the last table aloud, and did not stop at its end.

cards.name: Strike
cards.flavor:
The first cut the hamlets teach, made with whatever edge the hamlet owns. Marl's Hollow sends one climber a winter, chosen by the elders at the well, and the one chosen spends the last evening at the whetting post learning this and nothing more. The elders say a Forsaken needs only the one cut, since the marked learned a thousand and it did them no good.

— Marl's Hollow elders
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage.

cards.name: Defend
cards.flavor:
The first guard of the road, marked on cairn stones by climbers for climbers: two crossed lines, meaning hold. The mark does not say what to hold against, or for how long. The hamlets say it was cut by the first Forsaken to climb, before the Burning, when the ring was closed to them. Who those first climbers were, and what they climbed toward, the hamlets cannot agree.

— told at the Grave of the Nameless
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block.

cards.name: Footwork
cards.flavor:
Steps cut into the road by those who came before, and the way of moving that goes with them. The steps are too even to be natural and too worn to be recent. Climbers credit them to the Forsaken. They run on past the farthest point any Forsaken is known to have reached, and some lead out onto the viaducts, which are older than the kingdom.

Climbers before you cut steps. Use them.
— cairn-scratch
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Draw {draw} card.

cards.name: Evasive Guard
cards.flavor:
The ice-fishers' way of giving ground: a step sideways onto ice that will hold one person and not two. The lakes of the Pale Marches have not thawed since the Burning, and the fishers say the ice cracks all year round and gives only under a second pair of feet. They learned to trust the sound. Widow Arne of Sallow Lake says the sound changed last winter, and she has stopped fishing.

— ice-fishers' talk
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block, then roll to evade: on a success, gain Block equal to the dodge.

cards.name: Dodge Roll
cards.flavor:
A tumble across a shifting deck, learned from the ship-breakers of the Grave of Ships, who work on hulls that move with each tide. Gull-Bet's gang teaches it to anyone who pays. She says the hulls were already rotting at anchor when the trade stopped, and that on the night of the Burning every hold went warm at once. Her gang opened the holds the next spring, and she has not told anyone what was in them.

— ship-breakers' talk
cards.textTemplate: Roll to evade: on a success, gain Block from the dodge. Light: 1 Stamina. Medium: 2 Stamina, 1 Energy. Heavy: 3 Stamina, 2 Energy.

cards.name: Gorefire Slash
cards.flavor:
First cut of the Bastion's hired blades, set down in the years when the Wardens had more gates than sworn men to hold them. The drill has the edge wetted from the wielder's own forearm before the watch, so the steel goes out already red. The book calls this discipline, and adds that a sworn Warden never needed it. The page naming who first taught it is torn away below the words "the old sergeant".

— Warden's field-book
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {bleed} Bleed.

cards.name: Crimson Cleave
cards.flavor:
A wide, low cut for a gate choked with bodies, entered by the Fell Courtyard watch on the night the Bastion burned. The entry says the dead came up the Muster Stair in numbers the watch had no word for, and that this cut was the only one that answered them. It lists the watch as whole at the bell. The hand that wrote it changes halfway down the page.

— Fell Courtyard gate log
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies. Apply {bleed} Bleed to ALL.

cards.name: Shield Bash
cards.flavor:
Rim-work from the Wardens' shield line, drilled in the years when neighbours came to the Bastion's gate to argue the price of a spring. The book prefers the rim to the face, the face being gilded with the crest and too costly to dent. It notes that envoys of the Northern Holds were struck with it twice, and that both times the Holds paid. It does not say what they were paying for.

— Warden's field-book
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage.

cards.name: Quickstep
cards.flavor:
Short, flat steps for courtyard stone slick with moss, the way the Bastion's hired blades learned to move once the green came up between the flags and would not stop. Sellswords say the Wardens never taught it, because Wardens were never posted where the footing was worst. The steps are counted to the old dawn peal, which the Bell Keeper rings at an hour that no longer matches the light.

— as the sellswords tell it
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Draw {draw} card.

cards.name: Guard Counter
cards.flavor:
A Warden's answer to a blow already caught on the guard. The book teaches it as the proper order of things: the enemy commits, the Bastion replies, and the reply is always the larger. Wardens said the same of the Spring Wars, in which they claim never to have struck first. A copyist has added, in a smaller hand, that the Holds would tell it differently.

— Warden's field-book
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. If you have Block: deal {damage.2} instead.

cards.name: Iron Resolve
cards.flavor:
The standing order read out at the muster peal: a Warden holds until relieved, and relief comes from the bell. The bell-roll lists the names of those who held. After the Burning the list runs on for several pages in a hand the scribes did not know, and the names on those pages are ones the roll has no record of enlisting.

— Bastion bell-roll
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. If in Bulwark Stance: gain {block.2} instead.

cards.name: Serrated Blade
cards.flavor:
A saw-backed blade from the forges under the Bastion ridge, made for clearing briar and taken up by the Wardens when the Blight came out of the weald. The smiths say they filed the teeth for thornwood, not for men, and that the Wardens never paid for the change of use. How the briar learned to bleed is a question the smiths decline to take up.

— weald smiths' talk
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. If the target has Bleed: apply {bleed} more Bleed.

cards.name: Enter: Gorefire
cards.flavor:
The breaking stance, first of the two the Wardens taught. The book describes it as holding the flame in the blade. Its margins say more than its text: burns dressed, a sergeant's warning that the stance takes the hand if held too long, and a note that sellswords held it longer than Wardens, which the note gives as proof of their greed. The last line in the margin is smudged past reading.

— Warden's field-book
cards.textTemplate: Enter Gorefire Stance. Draw {draw} card.

cards.name: Enter: Bulwark
cards.flavor:
The holding stance, second of the two. The Wardens called the gate a wall a man could carry, and taught this as the way to carry it: low, square, shield set against the hinge side. The book claims that no gate held in this stance ever fell. The passage was written well before the Burning, and whether anyone has thought to correct it since is not clear from the ink.

— Warden's field-book
cards.textTemplate: Enter Bulwark Stance.

upgrade.textTemplate: Enter Bulwark Stance. Gain {block} extra Block.

cards.name: Riposte
cards.flavor:
A return taken off the guard, which the Citadel's fencing-masters claimed as their own and called too fine for field-born hands. The manual's example bout is fought on the bridges in the first year of the Mark Trade, between a Knight and an unnamed Warden. The text says the Knight won. The illustration beside it shows him on his back.

— Citadel fencing manual
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. If you have Block: deal {poiseDamage} Poise damage.

cards.name: Rend
cards.flavor:
A tearing cut for things of the weald that bleed black and stay standing. The entry is a late one, written after the Burning by whoever keeps the book now. It advises cutting the rot out of hounds and hamlet folk alike, and states that the rot came into the weald from outside, up the river road with the Court's traders. The ink is fresh and the hand is unsteady.

— Warden's field-book, late entry
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {bleed} Bleed. Gorefire: apply {bleed.2} more.

cards.name: Cleaving Blow
cards.flavor:
A heavy sweep taught in the weald hamlets for the winters when blight-hounds come down out of the lanternwood in packs. The elders say they learned it by watching the Wardens from outside the walls, since no Warden would teach a Forsaken anything. The Wardens called the weald their charge. The hamlets remember paying for that charge in spring grain, and remember what it bought.

— Marl's Hollow elders
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies. Deal {poiseDamage} Poise damage to ALL.

cards.name: Stomp
cards.flavor:
A heel brought down on a fallen enemy's chest, which the Wardens called unworthy and used regardless. Sellswords learned it in the Fell Courtyard, where the fallen seldom stayed down. They say the Wardens objected not to the blow but to being seen to deliver it. Several of the Bastion's older helms carry a heel-shaped dent, though whose heel is anyone's guess.

— sellswords' talk
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage.

cards.name: Rallying Standard
cards.flavor:
The Wardens' banner of the muster, raised when the bell rang the line into place. The book gives the drill in plain terms: raise the standard, sound the bell, log that the line held. The log of the last muster reads that the line held. The same page gives the hour as dawn, and the Bastion has not seen a dawn since the Burning.

— Warden's field-book
cards.textTemplate: At the start of your turn, gain 1 Strength and take 1 damage.

upgrade.textTemplate: At the start of your turn, gain 1 Strength.

cards.name: War Surgeon
cards.flavor:
The field practice of the Bastion's surgeon-wardens, who stitched wounds on the wall rather than below it. Their rule was that a Warden stitched standing remained a Warden, and one carried down to the stool was struck from the roll. The book credits them with a better record than the Chapel's physicians. The Chapel's own figures for those years burned with the Chapel.

— Warden's field-book
cards.textTemplate: Heal 2 HP for every 4 Bleed on all enemies. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Heal 2 HP for every 3 Bleed on all enemies. Exhaust.

cards.name: Hemorrhage
cards.flavor:
A second cut laid into a wound already open. The Court's surgeons, who studied such matters, recorded that Wardens bled longer than anyone else under the knife, and put it down to field-born blood running thin. The casebook gives no count of cases, only the conclusion, which the surgeons signed as a body in the ninth year of the Mark Trade.

— Court surgeons' casebook
cards.textTemplate: Double the target's Bleed. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Double the target's Bleed.

cards.name: Twinblade Flurry
cards.flavor:
Two short blades worked in turn, the habit of weald sellswords who could not afford a shield and would not carry a Warden's. The Bastion hired them for its narrow gates. Sellswords say part of their pay came as a mark on the wrist in place of coin, a right to the city's warmth. Those who took it are not around to confirm the story. Those who refused tell it often.

— sellswords' talk
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage {hits} times.

cards.name: Shieldwall
cards.flavor:
Rims locked edge to edge across the Fell Courtyard, the formation the Wardens were proudest of. The book credits it with holding the Bastion gate through three hungry winters of the Spring Wars, when Hold petitioners camped below the walls. It enters the price of the spring harvest in the same column as the petitioners it turned away.

— Warden's field-book
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. If in Bulwark Stance: gain 4 Block next turn.

cards.name: Kick Off
cards.flavor:
A boot to the chest that sends an enemy back down the Muster Stair. Sellswords learned it on those steps, which are steep enough that the fall does most of the work. They say the Wardens forbade it as common and had copied it within a season. What climbs the stair now tends to climb it again, and the sellswords who remain have stopped counting how often.

— sellswords' talk
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage.

cards.name: Warding Lunge
cards.flavor:
A guarded step forward that ends in the breaking stance, taught as the moment to stop holding and start taking ground. The book says a Warden should know the moment by the bell. After the Bellfoundry bell cracked, a new line was added beneath: know it by the smell of the courtyard. What that smell is supposed to be, the entry leaves to the reader.

— Warden's field-book
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Enter Gorefire Stance.

cards.name: Impale
cards.flavor:
A thrust that pins a fallen enemy to the ground. The weald hamlets learned it for the things that came out of the drowned hamlet in the first winter of the Blight, which got up again when left lying. Hamlet folk say a pinned thing stops. The Wardens would once have burned them, but the fire went into the Wardens that winter, and the hamlets never had any to spare.

— weald hamlet saying
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. If the target is Staggered: apply {bleed} Bleed.

cards.name: Warcry
cards.flavor:
The bell-roll shouted aloud where the bell could not be heard, a custom of the gates farthest from the Bellfoundry. The Wardens held that the roll had a power of its own, so long as it was read in order. Sellswords, who were not on it, learned to shout it anyway. The Bell Keeper is said to answer when he hears it, with the bell, which is cracked.

— Bastion bell-roll, marginal note
cards.textTemplate: Gain {strength} Strength. Draw {draw} card. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Gain {strength} Strength. Draw {draw} card.

cards.name: Executioner
cards.flavor:
A finishing blow as the Fell Warden taught it, before his leg went the way of the weald and his blade was ground down into a cane. The book gives his instruction in full and his reasons not at all. It states that he never struck a man already kneeling. The last page in his hand, dated the night of the Burning, is a list of kneeling men.

— Warden's field-book
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. If the target is Staggered: deal {damage.2} instead.

cards.name: Goreblood
cards.flavor:
The Wardens' word for the state a fighter reaches when enough of their own blood is on the ground that fear stops mattering. The book treats it as a virtue in sworn men and a vice in sellswords, though it describes the two in identical terms. It claims the state can be taught. The only instruction it offers is to keep standing.

— Warden's field-book
cards.textTemplate: Poise thresholds no longer increase after filling.

cards.name: Unbreakable
cards.flavor:
The order to hold the Fell Courtyard gate until relieved, as it stands in the gate log: dated, signed, and never countermanded. The entries go on past the Burning in the second hand, at the same hour each night. Who relieved the writer, or whether anyone came to, the log does not record.

— Fell Courtyard gate log
cards.textTemplate: Block no longer expires at the start of your turn. (Block capped at 30.)

upgrade.textTemplate: Block no longer expires at the start of your turn. (Block capped at 40.)

cards.name: Stitched Arms
cards.flavor:
A way of swinging a weapon lashed to the arm, copied from the Court's knights after their surgeons sewed them to their swords. The Citadel's record calls the stitching an honour: a knight's word made flesh, never to be set down. The record was written by the surgeons, and it treats the question of whether the knights were asked as settled.

— Citadel surgeons' record
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to a random enemy, scaling with Energy spent.

upgrade.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to a random enemy, scaling with Energy spent.

cards.name: Last Stand
cards.flavor:
The last entry in the Fell Courtyard gate log before the handwriting changes. One gate, one man, it reads, and the man is not named. The entry is written as though the writer expected nobody to need it. The count of the dead is given twice on the page, and the two counts do not agree.

— Fell Courtyard gate log
cards.textTemplate: Ethereal. Gain Block equal to your missing HP (max 20).

upgrade.textTemplate: Ethereal. Gain Block equal to your missing HP (max 30).

cards.name: Warrior's Vow
cards.flavor:
The contract read to sellswords hired for the Fell Courtyard: hold the gate until relieved, pay in advance. Weald sellswords treated a paid contract as sacred, having few other sacred things, and the Wardens thought them mercenary for it. The last contract on the roll was signed the week before the Burning. The space for the date of release is blank.

— Bastion hiring roll
cards.textTemplate: Innate. Enter Gorefire Stance. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Innate. Enter Gorefire Stance. Draw {draw} card. Exhaust.

cards.name: Ruinous Blow
cards.flavor:
The whole weight of the body brought down through the blade, which the book reserves for a gate where all else has failed. It calls this a Warden's last argument. It does not describe what becomes of the Warden afterward. The pages here are stained through, and the drill's final step can only be guessed at from what shows at the edges.

— Warden's field-book
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage.

cards.name: Bloodhunter's Strike
cards.flavor:
A strike aimed where the quarry is already bleeding, taught by the Bastion's kennelmaster before the hounds turned. The kennel book calls them the finest hounds in the three cities, trained on the scent of blood alone, and credits the Wardens with never setting them on the weald's own people. The hamlets' dogs, which were never trained, were found in those same kennels after the Burning.

— Bastion kennel book
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage, plus 1 for each Bleed on the target.

cards.name: Sanguine Pact
cards.flavor:
A soldier's bargain sworn at the Bastion's lesser shrine: blood spilled from an enemy is sworn to the one who spilled it. The Wardens held it a harmless custom of the field-born, like the harvest tithe. The Chapel called it a mockery of the Writing and fined the shrine. The fine is entered as paid, and the shrine was in use on the night of the Burning.

— Warden's field-book
cards.textTemplate: Whenever Bleed bursts on an enemy, gain 2 Strength.

cards.name: Goreslash
cards.flavor:
A short, deep cut from the Bastion's hired blades, who had no patience for the long forms of the Wardens' drill. Sellswords say a long cut belongs in songs, and that the songs about the Bastion were paid for by the Wardens. They sing their own verse about the Fell Courtyard. Most of its words are lost, but the tune is known on both sides of the wall.

— sellswords' talk
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {bleed} Bleed.

cards.name: Bracing Stance
cards.flavor:
Feet planted, shield braced against the Bastion's own wall: the stance recruits learned before they were trusted with either of the two proper ones. Drillmaster Hask, whom the book quotes at length, taught it for thirty winters. Her entries end the spring before the Burning with a list of recruits, a line drawn through every name but one, and that one scraped away.

— Warden's field-book
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. If in Bulwark Stance: gain {block.2} more.

cards.name: Flame to Blade
cards.flavor:
Lanternwood oil run along the edge and set alight, a practice the Wardens adopted late, once their plain steel no longer frightened what came out of the weald. The book is wary of it. It warns that the oil takes the sleeve before the enemy, and that the Chapel disapproved of Wardens carrying fire they had not been given. The warning about the sleeve is underlined twice.

— Warden's field-book
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. If already in Gorefire Stance: deal {damage.2} more. Enter Gorefire Stance.

cards.name: Iron Vow
cards.flavor:
The oath a Warden swore to the Bastion, sword hand on the gate. Sworn Wardens were marked at birth like any field-born citizen, and the oath was understood as a second promise laid over the first. Sellswords swore it without the first promise, and the Wardens held that this left them less bound. What it left them on the night of the Burning, the book does not say.

— Warden's field-book
cards.textTemplate: Whenever you lose HP, gain 3 Block.

cards.name: Blood Tithe
cards.flavor:
The harvest tithe of the weald, paid in blood at the Bastion's field-shrine in years when the grain failed. The Wardens administered it and called it voluntary. The tithe-roll records amounts and villages but no names, which the Wardens explained as a courtesy to the givers. The roll grows longer each year of the Mark Trade, and the villages it lists grow fewer.

— weald tithe-roll
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage, plus double the Bleed on the target.

cards.name: Poise Breaker
cards.flavor:
Two blows to the knee, which Drillmaster Hask taught as the answer to anything larger than a Warden. Her notes say a knight and a kennel hound bend in the same place, and she drew both. Beside them, in later ink, someone has drawn a third figure grown out of briar, and given it a name the book uses nowhere else.

— Warden's field-book
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage. If the target is Staggered: deal {poiseDamage.2} more Poise damage.

cards.name: Rondel Parry
cards.flavor:
A parry on the guard of a rondel dagger, favoured by the Bastion's older sellswords, who carried the short blade long after the Wardens stopped issuing it. They claim the rondels came from the Northern Holds as part of a year's tribute, and were worth more than the Bastion paid them in a season. The daggers are stamped with a crest the ring's heralds never recorded.

— sellswords' talk
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block and deal {poiseDamage} Poise damage.

cards.name: Sunderplate
cards.flavor:
A blow meant to split plate at the joints. The book says the Wardens designed it during the Mark Trade with the Court's knights in mind, "in case the Court forgets which flame keeps it fed". It records no occasion on which it was used. The entry is kept all the same, beside a sketch of a knight's gorget with the Court's crest scratched out.

— Warden's field-book
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage. If the target is Staggered: apply {bleed} Bleed.

cards.name: Brace
cards.flavor:
The crouch taught before either stance: knees bent, weight low, the body made ready to be struck. The book gives it the first page of the drill and calls it the one lesson all Wardens learned alike, sworn or hired, marked or not. It is among the few passages that treats sellswords as equals. A later hand has corrected it.

— Warden's field-book
cards.textTemplate: Enter Brace Stance.

upgrade.textTemplate: Enter Brace Stance. Gain {block} Block.

cards.name: Starstone Pebble
cards.flavor:
A chip of starstone of the kind the Observatory's apprentices were set to weigh and catalogue in their first winter. The Astronomer held that such stones were inert once cooled, and his catalogue says so throughout. The apprentices kept the drawers shut at night all the same. Their notes record frost forming on the labels, though never on the stones.

— Starwatch catalogue, apprentice notes
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Starstone: deal {damage.2} more.

cards.name: Comet Fragment
cards.flavor:
A broken piece of starstone thrown hard, the plainest working of the Starwatch and the first an apprentice was allowed to cast outside the lens gallery. The fragments came up the Basalt Stair in miners' sacks and were sold by weight. The Astronomer bought and catalogued each one. His catalogue passes from chart 41, which records a fall, to chart 42, which records a hearth, and does not account for the interval.

— Starwatch catalogue
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage.

cards.name: Starblade Phalanx
cards.flavor:
A rank of blades ground from a single stone and cast one after another. The apprentices found that blades cut from the same stone answered one another in sequence, the second truer than the first. The Starwatch recorded this as a property of the stone. The Chapel's censor, reviewing the record, struck out "answered" and wrote "rang". The apprentices went on using the first word.

— Starwatch log, censored copy
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Starstone: deal {damage.2} again.

cards.name: Crystal Barrier
cards.flavor:
A pane of starstone raised before the one who works it, cut on the same principle as the Observatory's great lens. The lens cracked in the frost of the eclipse and went on holding the light. The Astronomer put this down to the quality of his grinding. Maud Vell, who ground it, said the crack had closed a little by morning, and would not grind another.

— Starwatch log
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Starstone: {block.2} more.

cards.name: Star Shower
cards.flavor:
A sheaf of small lights called down in sequence. The Starwatch log for one autumn vigil counts forty falls in a single night, none of which reached the ground warm. The log treats the count as ordinary. The apprentice who kept it wrote in the margin to ask where forty falls could come from in one night, and the answer beside it, in the Astronomer's hand, has been cut from the page.

— Starwatch log
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage {hits} times. Starstone: one more hit of {damage.2}.

cards.name: Scholar's Insight
cards.flavor:
The apprentices' habit of copying a chart twice, on the principle that the second copy is the true one. The Astronomer approved of it as discipline. The two copies of chart 9 differ in a single figure, and the Starwatch never settled which was right. The figure gives the distance from the three hearths to a point on the coast, and both copies left the Observatory with the apprentice who stole the charts.

— apprentice's letter
cards.textTemplate: Draw {draw} cards.

cards.name: Frost Veil
cards.flavor:
A veil of rime drawn over the one who works it, first recorded on the Observatory's upper terrace on the night of the eclipse, when the terrace froze in the space of a breath. The instruments stopped together. An apprentice named Hollis logged the hour from the stopped clock and wrote beside it that he did not trust it. Someone has since corrected the hour, in a hand that is not the Astronomer's, and given no reason.

— Starwatch log, eclipse night
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Apply {frost} Frost.

cards.name: Star Slicer
cards.flavor:
A fragment split along its grain and thrown in pieces. Starstone splits cleanly along lines the lens-grinders could see and the miners could not. The grinders took this as a sign the stone had been worked before it ever fell, an idea the Astronomer called sentimental. He kept a split fragment on his desk nonetheless, turned so the grain faced the window.

— lens-grinders' talk
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage {hits} times. Starstone: one more hit of {damage.2}.

cards.name: Starstone Ward
cards.flavor:
A slab of starstone stood upright as a shield, after the fashion of the Observatory's doors, which were cut long before the Starwatch by builders whose name the Chapel did not keep. Starstone stays cold when all else warms, and the apprentices trusted it for that. They also believed the doors had not been built to open from the inside. The Chapel's inventory lists the doors as ornamental.

— Starwatch inventory
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Starstone: apply {weak} Weak.

cards.name: Starlance
cards.flavor:
A beam of light forced through a starstone lens onto a single point. The Starwatch found it by accident, when the great lens scorched a line across the chart-room table. The Astronomer had the table kept as it was and recorded that the line ran true to the south-west. The table is kept as it was, and the line on it has lengthened since.

— Starwatch log
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Starstone: {damage.2} instead.

cards.name: Twinkling
cards.flavor:
A small light drawn from a star that varies. The Astronomer recorded its variation nightly for many years and drew no conclusion from it, which he described as his rule. His apprentices said he broke the rule once, in the last spring before the Burning, when he spent three nights on that star alone. The charts for those nights are not in the series.

— apprentice's letter
cards.textTemplate: Draw {draw} card. Starstone: gain {gainEnergy} Energy.

cards.name: Frost Nova
cards.flavor:
A burst of cold that rings the one who works it, modelled on the rings of frozen ash the miners found around fresh falls on the caldera floor. Coll, a foreman who sold fragments to the Starwatch, told the apprentices the ash froze before the stone landed, not after. The Astronomer told him miners were unreliable witnesses, then bought his next fragment at double the price.

— reach miners' talk
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {frost} Frost. Starstone: apply {frost.2} more.

cards.name: Starstone Arc
cards.flavor:
An arc of force cast from starstone, the working the apprentices used to measure how far the stone would reach. The arc was measured three times and the stone found to have moved between readings. The log calls the movement an error in the apparatus. The apparatus was replaced, and the log records the same error each month until its entries end at the eclipse.

— Starwatch log
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Starstone: apply {vulnerable} Vulnerable.

cards.name: Lucidity
cards.flavor:
A clearing of the head for work, which the Starwatch practised on the one clear night in forty that the reach allowed. The Astronomer worked through such nights without sleep and required his apprentices to do the same. They believed he saw more on those nights than the charts show, and wrote it down somewhere else. The Starwatch holds only the charts.

— apprentice's letter
cards.textTemplate: Gain {gainEnergy} Energy. Draw {draw} card.

cards.name: Stargazer
cards.flavor:
The long watch at the eyepiece. The Astronomer kept it for a hundred years by his own count, and in that time wrote a great deal about the coal's dimming and nothing about what the dimming meant. The Chapel admired his restraint. I have written home before that the old man is watching something he has already decided not to describe. I will not write it again.

— apprentice's letter
cards.textTemplate: At the start of your turn, gain Starstone Charge.

cards.name: Astral Armor
cards.flavor:
A mantle of cold light that settles over the one who works it, named for Starwatch Terrace on the Drowned Coast, which the Astronomer had paved in starstone so his apprentices could measure the new tower's draw. The paving never warmed in summer and the salt spray never dried on it. I was sent to bless the stones, and blessed them without incident. I ask to be posted elsewhere.

— Chapel visitation report
cards.textTemplate: At the end of your turn, gain 4 Block.

upgrade.textTemplate: At the end of your turn, gain 8 Block.

cards.name: Moonrend Cut
cards.flavor:
A crescent stroke from the curved blades of the Observatory's night-porters, who walked the Basalt Stair with lanterns. The porters claimed the moon's passage over the caldera showed them where to cut. The Starwatch called this folklore and employed them anyway. Their blades turn up now in the lower galleries, sometimes in the hands of porters who are no longer entirely themselves.

— Starwatch log
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage.

cards.name: Meteorite
cards.flavor:
A heavy stone called down on a single enemy. The Starwatch recovered its largest fragment from below the Basalt Stair and recorded that it weighed more than its size allowed. The miners who carried it up said it weighed more at the top of the stair than at the bottom. The Astronomer had it weighed at both ends and entered the results in cipher.

— Starwatch catalogue
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Starstone: {damage.2} instead.

cards.name: Meteor Swarm
cards.flavor:
Many falls called at once. Chart 43 records two falls on a single night, and the Starwatch sent miners to both sites, who found no crater at either. The Astronomer entered both falls regardless, on the grounds that his lens could not be wrong. A third mark on chart 43, in another ink, is not explained anywhere in the catalogue.

— Starwatch catalogue
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies. Starstone: {damage.2} again.

cards.name: Gravity Well
cards.flavor:
A pull that drags enemies off their footing, named for the Observatory's great pendulum. The pendulum swung true for most of the Starwatch's history. In the years the Spire was building, it began to lean toward the coast and did not recover. The Astronomer recorded the lean monthly, put it down to settling in the tower's foundations, and ordered an inspection. The inspection report is blank.

— Starwatch log
cards.textTemplate: Apply {vulnerable} Vulnerable to ALL enemies. Starstone: apply {weak} Weak to ALL.

cards.name: Azure Coil
cards.flavor:
A coil of blue light that gathers around whoever is working it, first noticed around apprentices reciting the star tables aloud in rhythm. The Starwatch claims the rhythm draws it. This office holds that the recited tables are in an old script and should not be spoken, and has ordered the recitation stopped. The coil was observed around the same apprentices the following night.

— Chapel censor's report
cards.textTemplate: Whenever you play a Skill, gain 2 Block.

cards.name: Astral Cleave
cards.flavor:
A cut of cold force, first seen when a falling fragment passed through the lens gallery and sheared the telescope cleanly in two before cooling on the floor. The Astronomer entered the event as a fall. His lens-grinder, Maud Vell, who had been standing at the eyepiece, described it as a throw. She was dismissed at the end of that season.

— Starwatch log
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage. Starstone: deal {damage.2} more.

cards.name: Radiant Spray
cards.flavor:
A flare of light thrown wide across the field. The Starwatch recorded one such flare in the years the Spire was building, bright enough to light all the Observatory's terraces at once, and noted that the apprentices on duty lost their sight for several days. The log gives no source for the flare. When their sight returned, the apprentices were asked not to discuss it.

— Starwatch log
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} to ALL enemies. Apply {vulnerable} Vulnerable to ALL. Starstone: deal {damage.2} to ALL again.

cards.name: Supernova
cards.flavor:
The brightest working in the charts, and the last the Starwatch recorded. The Astronomer's final predictive chart forecasts a light strong enough to burn the paper it is drawn on. The Starwatch took it for a prediction about a star. The chart is unsigned and undated, and the apprentices who filed the series swore it was not among the sheets they left on his desk.

— Starwatch catalogue
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies, scaling with Energy spent.

upgrade.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies, scaling with Energy spent.

cards.name: Time Dilation
cards.flavor:
A slowing of the moment, named for the night of the eclipse. By the Starwatch's reckoning the eclipse lasted one night. By the Observatory clock it has not ended. Anselm, who kept the clock, refused to reset it and was found beside it when the others came up, in the position he had held when the light went. The clock has not been reset.

— Starwatch log
cards.textTemplate: Gain {gainEnergy} Energy. Draw {draw} cards. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Gain {gainEnergy} Energy. Draw {draw} cards.

cards.name: Starstone Kris
cards.flavor:
A wavy dagger of starstone, carried by apprentices for rough work in the lower galleries. The apprentice who owned the first of them wrapped it in cloth and found the cloth frosted by morning. The Starwatch recorded that the kris held its cold whether carried or not. The apprentice noted, on a separate leaf, that it was coldest in the Astronomer's presence.

— Starwatch log
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Starstone: draw {draw} card and deal {damage.2} again.

cards.name: Constellation
cards.flavor:
A working that draws on three stars at once, patterned on the constellation behind the Goldbough's crest: three flames on three twigs. The Chapel taught that the crest came first and the stars were named after it. The Starwatch's oldest star-plate, cut before the kingdom, shows the same three stars with a faint fourth beside them. The Chapel's copy of the plate leaves it out.

— Starwatch catalogue, oldest plate
cards.textTemplate: Whenever you gain Starstone Charge, deal 4 damage to a random enemy.

cards.name: Starfall Beam
cards.flavor:
A column of falling light, modelled on a fall the Astronomer charted in advance. He predicted where it would strike on the caldera rim and sent no warning to the mine camps there. His margin notes that the camps were unmarked and absent from the Court's maps, and that he had therefore counted the ground as empty. The margin gives the fall's weight to the grain, and the camps' number not at all.

— Astronomer's chart margin
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies. Starstone: {damage.2} instead.

cards.name: Starcaller
cards.flavor:
A working that calls falls in number, as the apprentices practised it in the lens gallery. The apprentices chanted the star tables in rhythm while practising it, and on the night it was first attempted the Starwatch recorded eleven falls. The Astronomer entered the chanting and the falls in the same line and drew no connection between them. He never drew connections, the apprentices said.

— apprentice's letter
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage, scaling with Energy spent. Starstone: deal {damage.2} more.

upgrade.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage, scaling with Energy spent. Starstone: deal {damage.2} more.

cards.name: Umbral Ward
cards.flavor:
A ward of shadow cast from starstone, named for the eclipse, during which the Observatory cast no shadow at all. The Starwatch recorded the absence as a curiosity of the light. The apprentices on the terrace that night reported that they cast shadows as usual, but that their shadows fell toward the Observatory rather than away from it.

— Starwatch log
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Starstone: {block.2} instead.

cards.name: Waxing Moon
cards.flavor:
A working that grows night by night, named for the moon-table the Starwatch kept alongside its ember-tables. In the last decade before the Burning the two tables moved in step: each night the moon grew, the coal in the Crown dimmed by the same measure. The Astronomer noted the correspondence, called it coincidence, and stopped keeping the moon-table.

— Starwatch tables
cards.textTemplate: At the start of your turn, apply 2 Vulnerable to ALL enemies.

cards.name: Shooting Shard
cards.flavor:
A small fall called down quickly, too small for the charts. The Starwatch left falls of this size unrecorded, holding that a star too faint to mark the lens was not worth the ink. The reach miners kept their own tally of small falls, scratched on the walls of the lower galleries. The log mentions the tally once, to dismiss it, and gives a figure far higher than its own.

— Starwatch log
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Starstone: deal {damage.2} more.

cards.name: Warding Star
cards.flavor:
A guarding light fixed above the one who works it, named for the star the apprentices called the Fixed Lamp, which hung over the coast and did not move with the others. The Starwatch took it for a flaw in the lens and reground the lens twice. The star stayed where it was. Once the Spire was finished, the log stops using the name and refers to it only as "the error".

— Starwatch log
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Starstone: draw {draw} card.

cards.name: Star Path
